spec_facts.statement: In FIPS 203 pseudocode, arrays of integers modulo m are added coordinate-wise: for X,Y in Z_m^l, the statement W <- X + Y yields W[i] = X[i] + Y[i] for all i.
spec_facts.verification_relevance: candidate specification fact for later range checking and candidate algorithm-to-code trace item for polynomial addition loops.

evidence_references.excerpt: The statements Z <- a·X and W <- X + Y will result in two arrays Z,W in Z_m^l, with the property that Z[i] = a·X[i] and W[i] = X[i] + Y[i] for all i.
evidence_references.supports_claim: Arrays of integers modulo m are added coordinate-wise in pseudocode.

spec_facts.statement: A polynomial in R_q is represented in pseudocode by a length-256 coefficient array over Z_q, with entry f[i] equal to the i-th polynomial coefficient f_i.
spec_facts.verification_relevance: candidate specification fact for later C-level array-shape assumptions and coefficient-wise reasoning.

evidence_references.excerpt: An element f of R_q is a polynomial ... and will be represented in pseudocode by the array (f0, f1, …, f255) in Z_q^256 ... The i-th entry of the array f will thus contain the i-th coefficient of the polynomial f (i.e., f[i] = f_i).
evidence_references.supports_claim: A polynomial in R_q is represented as a length-256 coefficient array over Z_q.

spec_facts.statement: An element of T_q is also represented in pseudocode by a length-256 coefficient array over Z_q, with index mapping ghat[2i] = ghat_{i,0} and ghat[2i+1] = ghat_{i,1}.

evidence_references.excerpt: Such an algebraic object will be represented in pseudocode by the array ... in Z_q^256 ... the mapping between array entries and coefficients is ghat[2i] = ghat_i,0 and ghat[2i+1] = ghat_i,1.

spec_facts.statement: Addition in both R_q and T_q is done coordinate-wise, and in pseudocode this is performed by addition of the corresponding coefficient arrays as in equation (2.3).

functions.name: mlk_poly_add
functions.role: In-place coefficient-wise addition of polynomial b into polynomial r without modular reduction inside the function body; intended repository counterpart of ML-KEM polynomial addition used in K-PKE.Encrypt before later reduction.
inputs: r: pointer to mutable mlk_poly whose coeffs array is updated in place
b: pointer to const mlk_poly whose coeffs array is read
outputs: Post-state r->coeffs[k] equals old r->coeffs[k] + b->coeffs[k] for all k in 0..MLKEM_N-1, under stated preconditions
modified_memory: memory slice of *r only; b is read-only

evidence_references.excerpt: void mlk_poly_add(mlk_poly *r, const mlk_poly *b) __contract__( requires(memory_no_alias(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(memory_no_alias(b, sizeof(mlk_poly))) requires(forall(k0, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k0] + b->coeffs[k0] <= INT16_MAX)) requires(forall(k1, 0, MLKEM_N, (int32_t) r->coeffs[k1] + b->coeffs[k1] >= INT16_MIN)) ensures(forall(k, 0, MLKEM_N, r->coeffs[k] == old(*r).coeffs[k] + b->coeffs[k])) assigns(memory_slice(r, sizeof(mlk_poly))) );
evidence_references.supports_claim: Signature, preconditions, postcondition, and write-set of mlk_poly_add.

evidence_references.excerpt: for (i = 0; i < MLKEM_N; i++) ... { /* The preconditions imply that the addition stays within int16_t. */ r->coeffs[i] = (int16_t)(r->coeffs[i] + b->coeffs[i]); }
evidence_references.supports_claim: Implementation performs element-wise in-place addition over all coefficients with explicit int16_t cast.
